cards.text: Zedekiah son of Josiah has just started his reign as king of Judah. Right at the beginning, the LORD gives a message to His prophet Jeremiah, and Jeremiah tells us about it himself. And friend, this message starts with an arts and crafts project.

cards.question: What does the LORD tell Jeremiah to make out of leather straps and put on his neck?

cards.text: A yoke. On his NECK. I wore a mixing bowl on my head for one afternoon, and not ONE baker took me seriously.
Envoys have come to Jerusalem to see King Zedekiah. They're from five nations: Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyre and Sidon.

cards.question: Through these envoys from five nations, who does the LORD tell Jeremiah to send word to?

cards.text: And the message from the LORD of Hosts starts at the very beginning. By His great power and outstretched arm, He made the earth, and the people and animals on it.

cards.question: Since God made the earth, who does He say He gives it to?
So right now, whose authority does God place all these lands under?

cards.text: God calls him "My servant," and He even makes the beasts of the field subject to him. That man's chain of command goes all the way down to the field mice.
All nations will serve Nebuchadnezzar, and his son, and his grandson.

cards.question: True or false: God says Babylon will stay on top forever.

cards.text: Nope. When the time of his own land comes, many nations and great kings will enslave him. Even the biggest empire has a timer on it, and friend, I KNOW timers.

cards.question: True or false: God says any nation that won't serve Nebuchadnezzar will be punished by sword and famine and plague.
Jeremiah's leather yoke is a picture of the nations ___ the king of Babylon.

cards.text: Then comes a warning for those five kings. Don't listen to your prophets, your diviners, your dream interpreters, your mediums or your sorcerers.

cards.question: What are all those voices telling the five kings?

answers.text: You will not serve Babylon's king
Babylon's king will set you free
Your gods will fight for you

cards.question: God says those voices prophesy a ___ that will get the nations removed from their land.

cards.text: God says He'll banish them, and they'll perish. Those advisers are like a GPS that says "turn left" and points you straight into the lake.

cards.question: True or false: The nation that puts its neck under Babylon's yoke and serves him gets to stay in its own land.

cards.text: Then Jeremiah takes the same message to Zedekiah king of Judah. Same yoke, same neck, brand new audience.

cards.question: Jeremiah tells Zedekiah and his people to put their necks under Babylon's yoke, serve, and ___.

cards.text: Then he asks why Zedekiah and his people should die by sword, famine and plague. That's the prophet version of "Why are we doing this the HARD way?"

cards.question: True or false: Jeremiah tells Zedekiah to listen to the prophets who say he must not serve the king of Babylon.
What does the LORD say about the prophets telling Zedekiah not to serve Babylon?

answers.text: He sent them to test Judah

cards.text: And yet they're prophesying falsely in His name. That's like a guy showing up at my bakery saying "Papa Dorin sent me," and I have NEVER seen this man in my life.

cards.question: What does God warn will happen to Zedekiah's people and those prophets together?

cards.text: Then Jeremiah turns to the priests and all the people. Their prophets have been making a promise about the articles from the house of the LORD that are in Babylon.

cards.question: What are those prophets promising about the articles from the LORD's house?

answers.text: They'll be brought back very soon
They'll be melted down in Babylon
They'll be sold off to Egypt

cards.question: Jeremiah calls that promise a lie and says, "Serve the king of Babylon and live!" Then he asks why this city should become what?

cards.text: Then Jeremiah throws down a challenge. If they really are prophets and the word of the LORD is with them, let them plead with the LORD of Hosts.

cards.question: If those prophets are the real thing, what should they plead with the LORD for?

answers.text: That the articles still left stay put
That the yoke on Judah breaks

cards.text: You say you can get the cookies back? Okay. Start by guarding the ones still sitting on the counter.

cards.question: The pillars, the sea, the bases and the rest still in Jerusalem were left behind when Nebuchadnezzar carried a king of Judah into exile. Which one?
True or false: When Nebuchadnezzar carried Jeconiah off, he took all the nobles of Judah and Jerusalem into exile too.
So what does the LORD of Hosts say will happen to the articles still left in Jerusalem?

answers.text: They'll stay safe in the temple

cards.text: They'll stay in Babylon until the day God attends to them again. Not the prophets' day. HIS day.

cards.question: True or false: God says the articles from His house will be lost in Babylon for good.

cards.text: Then He'll bring them back and restore them to this place. And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend, because this yoke story is NOT finished.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 3 quotes "Why are we doing this the HARD way?", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: This story card tells no new part of the passage. It repeats the yoke from card 2 and only adds a joke. The joke also suggests no one took Jeremiah seriously, which the text doesn't say.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: Card 8 says the prophets have been 'making a promise' about the articles. A promise is good news, so the two wrong answers ('melted down in Babylon', 'sold off to Egypt') are ruled out before the baker picks.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The question asks why the city should become something, which signals a bad outcome. 'A fortress' and 'A kingdom' are good outcomes, so they aren't believable and 'A ruin' stands out.

rule.text: Wrong answers for what someone does or says only need to be believable.

findings.problem: This story card adds no new part of the passage. It restates the 27:18 challenge already answered on card 12, as a joke only.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The card cites Jeremiah 27:19-20, but the right answer (Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim) is only in 27:20.

rule.text: A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.

findings.problem: Saying the articles will stay in Babylon 'until the day God attends to them again' gives away the answer to card 18 (whether they're lost in Babylon for good).

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The 'story isn't over' line nearly copies the doc's example ('And that's where we'll leave it for now... friend... this story's not done') instead of being a new line.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop: 7 of 11 choice cards are multiple choice, with 3 true or false and only 1 fill in the blank.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
